text:
maria: throwing this here — production infer svc started returning 503s ~10m ago after an autoscaler GPU eviction. pods look Terminating but traffic still hitting them per our app logs. any quick ideas?

jon: can you paste `kubectl get endpointslices -n infer svc/infer-headless -o yaml` and `kubectl get endpoints -n infer svc/infer-headless -o wide`? suspect endpointslice vs kube-proxy sync lag.

maria: running those now — here's the relevant slice (redacted):
```
apiVersion: discovery.k8s.io/v1
kind: EndpointSlice
metadata:
  name: infer-headless-abc123
  namespace: infer
endpoints:
  - addresses: [10.240.5.9]  # node that was drained 9m ago
    conditions: {ready: true}
  - addresses: [10.240.6.10]
    conditions: {ready: true}
```
endpoints shows just the service with no addresses on pod list (empty). kube-proxy logs on node show: `failed to sync endpoints for svc infer-headless: no endpoints` but iptables still has DNAT to 10.240.5.9 :

sam: sounds like kube-proxy didn't purge the NAT rule after endpoints removed. we hit this during a spot-drain earlier when conntrack entries + kube-proxy iptables race kept traffic flowing to evicted pod IPs. check `conntrack -L | grep 10.240.5.9` and `iptables -t nat -S | grep 10.240.5.9`

lee: also saw CoreDNS WARNs around the same time: `proxy: upstream failed, cached NX` — headless svc lookups sometimes return SRV records that don't match endpointslice state if kube-proxy/url-proxy races. could be the client caching SRV + conntrack combo.

infra-bot: cluster-autoscaler: cordon/evict triggered for node gpu-spot-usw2-17 at 1977776960 (reason: GPU-eviction, reclaim).

jon: what's kube-proxy mode on the affected node? iptables or ipvs? `ps -ef | grep kube-proxy` and `kubectl -n kube-system get ds kube-proxy -o yaml` — ipvs has different sync semantics; we saw earlier ipvs kube-proxy dropping endpoint deletions when ipset updates race with eviction.

maria: kube-proxy is iptables on those nodes. ran conntrack check — lots of ESTABLISHED entries for 10.240.5.9. iptables -t nat shows a chain with a DNAT to that ip for the headless clusterIP.

sam: conntrack will keep NAT path until flows expire. but kube-proxy should have removed the DNAT rule when endpoints cleared. can you share kube-proxy logs for that node around 1977776960-1977777000? simple restart of kube-proxy on the node might force a resync (fast workaround).

maria: pulling logs now — kube-proxy complained about `failed to remove iptables rule: device or resource busy` repeatedly.

ops-sre: we hit this pattern before. action plan: 1) canary restart kube-proxy on two nodes in the impacted AZ, 2) add an alert for endpointslice addresses pointing to nodes in NotReady/cordoned state, 3) open follow-up to harden kube-proxy resync path during evictions. anyone object to live restart?

jon: +1 for canary restart. also add an alert for endpoint count mismatch between Endpoints and EndpointSlice resource for headless svcs. that would've fired earlier.

maria: doing canary now on gpu-spot-usw2-18 (not the one that was drained). will report back in 2m.

deploy-bot: rolling restart initiated: daemonset/kube-proxy on node gpu-spot-usw2-18 (user: maria).

maria: restarted kube-proxy on gpu-spot-usw2-18 -> iptables resynced and DNAT to 10.240.5.9 cleared. traffic to infer-headless returned to normal. conntrack still shows old entries but new connections go to healthy pods.

sam: good. short-term root cause: kube-proxy hitting `device or resource busy` while trying to remove iptables rules during eviction, leaving stale DNAT rules until manual resync. long-term: we should add a resync job after large-scale node drains and backport any kube-proxy fixes.

lee: added note: also saw a handful of SERVFAILs from coredns while this was happening — probably due to pod IPs being temporarily inconsistent. recommend an eval of DNS caching TTLs for headless services.

ops-sre: created ticket INFRA-1132: "kube-proxy stale NAT rules after GPU evictions" with triage steps + alerting proposals. assigning to eng-infra. next steps: implement canary kube-proxy restart playbook, create alert, and test on staging with forced evictions.

maria: thanks all. leaving thread open until alerts added and playbook merged. :thumbsup:
